explain: Read the rules in order. 1. fetch runs first: v1 is free, so it loads an item. 2. exec runs and sees v1 set and v2 free: it moves the item to stage 2. 3. drain runs and sees v2 set: with out_ready high the consumer takes it. A new item passes through both stages and out within one cycle, so v1 and v2 are clear at the end of every cycle. out_valid, which interfaces computes at the start of the cycle, stays 0 for the whole run: the items stream through and are consumed unseen. fetch fires just as often, but the registers no longer separate the stages. With later stages first, each item spends a cycle in each register, and the consumer sees every item.
